queries: Faith and Fate: Limits of Transformers on Compositionality GPT-4 multiplication accuracy arxiv
GPT-4 technical report human-level performance benchmarks

sources_considered.why: A 2023 study measuring GPT-4 and ChatGPT accuracy on multi-digit multiplication.
Its abstract describes LLMs as strong on many tasks but reliant on subgraph matching (pattern matching).
The GPT-4 technical report gives human-level exam performance, evidence of strong learned pattern use.
Its table shows GSM-8K at 92% with chain of thought, relevant context on word-problem maths. It has no clean quotable sentence, so it is noted in the gaps.

receipt.public_excerpt: Yet, off-the-shelf ChatGPT and GPT4 achieve only 55% and 59% accuracies on this task, respectively (§3).

evidence_items.explanation: GPT-4, tested from January to May 2023, got 3-digit by 3-digit multiplication wrong about 41% of the time, a task a calculator never misses. This supports 'lousy' at arithmetic.

receipt.public_excerpt: transformer LLMs solve compositional tasks by reducing multi-step compositional reasoning into linearized subgraph matching, without necessarily developing systematic problem-solving skills.

evidence_items.explanation: The authors find LLMs succeed by matching learned sub-patterns rather than by running systematic procedures. That matches the claim's contrast between pattern matching and arithmetic.

receipt.public_excerpt: GPT-4 exhibits human-level performance on various professional and academic benchmarks, including passing a simulated bar exam with a score around the top 10% of test takers.

evidence_items.explanation: Human-level scores on many text benchmarks show that LLMs were strong at some pattern-based tasks in 2023. This supports the 'great at some kinds of pattern matching' half.

unresolved_gaps: The arithmetic tests cited use integer multiplication, not floating point numbers specifically.

With chain-of-thought prompting, GPT-4 scored highly on grade-school word problems (GSM-8K 92% in its technical report), and LLMs paired with code tools could compute exactly. Both soften 'lousy' for tool-assisted or simple-number use.
